headline: A three-level `styled(Component)` chain is the boundary `@yak/solid`'s folding cannot cross, and the cost lands in Solid's own component machinery: 4.39 of its 5.97 ms per render, against 0.957 ms of yak's own code.

microbench.why: `next-yak` concatenates the chain into one wrapper carrying all three classes and leads at 1.39M renders/s, just ahead of its own no-fold lane at 1.37M and `cnfast` at 1.35M. `yak-solid` falls to 241,000 for a reason its own code cannot explain: it books 0.957 ms of lib self-time while 4.39 ms sits in the framework bucket. Folding rewrites a `styled.tag` usage into a plain element but never a `styled(Component)` one, so every instance goes through `createComponent` and `Dynamic`, and Solid builds a component with a reactive scope for a tree that will never update. `emotion` at 426,000 loses to per-instance serialization instead.

autocannon.why: `next-yak` holds 1,180 req/s and `vanilla` 1,110. `yak-solid` serves 205 req/s, below `panda` at 255, because the per-element component instantiation happens inside every request and there is nothing to amortize.

attribution.why: `next-yak` at 0.817 ms carries 0.467 ms of lib self-time for one folded wrapper. `cn` at 0.951 ms and `cnfast` at 1.17 ms both cache the three-level merge, and their gap to `tailwind-merge` at 1.82 ms — 1.2 ms of it inside tailwind-merge itself — is what a cached merger is worth on repeated class lists. `yak-solid`'s 5.97 ms is 74% framework: `@solidjs/signals` and `@solidjs/web` doing scope setup per element, the price of the unfolded wrapper rather than a cost yak charges itself.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` claims the markup in 34.1 ms with no tree to build. `yak-solid` needs 70.9 ms for the same DOM because hydration walks the same three component layers the SSR pass had to instantiate. The React lanes cluster near 50 ms, `vanilla` reads 90.4 ms in this battery, and `emotion` trails at 110 ms.

inp.why: `yak-solid` at 3.4 ms and `vanilla-solid` at 3.5 ms against roughly 7.5 ms for the React lanes, on the standing caveat that React re-renders here with unchanged props and writes nothing while the Solid lanes' value change really updates the text. Within the React field `bamboo` at 5.4 ms leads and only `goober` at 11 ms separates upward.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 22.0 ms and `yak-solid` in 52.2 ms — the 30 ms between them is the same three-component instantiation the SSR number exposes, now paid in the browser. Every React lane sits between 73.8 ms and 108 ms, where layout dominates and composition depth barely registers.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane, in a narrow band around 0.13 ms. Three levels of composition change what runs in JavaScript, never what the style engine has to match.

payload.why: `vanilla` is the floor at 3,044 gz B. `yak-solid` reaches 9,105 B, of which the markup carries Solid's per-element hydration keys: the unfolded chain gives each instance its own id namespace, so the keys multiply exactly where folding failed. `styled-components` at 16,514 B and `cn` at 16,503 B sit at the other end for a different reason, shipping 13.5 kB and 13.1 kB of library JS.

nsweep.why: `next-yak` holds 2.76 ms at 4,000 instances against 3.03 ms for `vanilla`, so a folded chain has no slope of its own. `yak-solid` reaches 21.0 ms — the steepest line in the case, because the per-element component instantiation scales one-for-one with n.

crossCase: Bracketed by the Examples `compose-1` and `compose-6`. `next-yak` runs the three depths at 2.11M, 1.39M and 1.50M renders/s, so its chain flattens at construction and depth is free after the first level. `yak-solid` runs 5.08M, 241,000 and 236,000: folding covers the depth-1 usage completely and stops dead at the first `styled(Component)`, and the extra levels after that cost almost nothing on top.
